title: Conveyance duty phased out in favour of general rates (ACT)
summary: The ACT began a 20-year program in its 2012-13 Budget to abolish conveyance (stamp) duty, cutting duty rates every year and replacing the revenue with higher general rates, an annual tax on land. The first lower rates took effect on 6 June 2012.

instruments.title: Duties Act 1999 (ACT)
instruments.provisions: conveyance duty rates, cut each year

instruments.title: Rates Act 2004 (ACT)
instruments.provisions: general rates, raised to replace duty

commenced.what: First reduced conveyance duty rates under the tax reform program

direction_rationale: Replacing a transaction tax with a broad annual land tax lowers the cost of moving home and lets property change hands more easily; Treasury estimates conveyancing duty costs 72 cents of efficiency per extra dollar raised, against close to nothing for a broad land tax.

verified.notes: The 6 June 2012 date is from the ACT 2012-13 Budget taxation reform paper, as quoted in search results; the ACT Treasury site reset automated connections, so the paper was not read in full.

assessment.summary: Swaps stamp duty for an annual land tax, step by step over 20 years. One of the most efficient tax reforms in Australia: it lowers the cost of moving home and lets property change hands more easily.

marks.reason: Replaces a highly distorting transaction tax with a broad annual land tax.
Lowers the cost of moving home, including to take a better job.
